To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the combination of zidovudine (ZDV) with dideoxycytidine (ddC) is superior to the combination of ZDV with dideoxyinosine (ddl) and that ddC alone has a greater effect than either ddC or ddl in combination with ZDV.
HIV proteinase is essential to the replication of HIV and is an excellent target for drug design.
HIV-1 proteinase is essential for the maturation of the viral core and that the enzyme can be inactivated by inhibitors that are potent and selective.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of drugs that are more potent, have a broader spectrum of activity, and are less prone to the development of resistance.
the design, synthesis, biological evaluation, and mechanism of action of compounds with novel mechanisms of action against HIV.
the development of novel antiviral drugs, and the development of new approaches to treatment of HIV disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have no idea what the future of HIV disease treatment will be, but that we are working hard on the problem.
we are at the beginning of the end of AIDS.
the future holds a variety of new agents, each with a specific mechanism of action.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the development of new drugs is progressing, but that there are still major gaps to be bridged.
we have developed a new class of compounds that are potent and specific inhibitors of HIV-1 and HIV-2 RTs.
the HIV proteinase inhibitors, although promising, are not yet ready for clinical use.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the immune system is the key to the control of HIV infection.
the virus can mutate in a way that can overcome the effects of the drug.
the virus is not going to be eradicated by any single drug, but by combinations of drugs that attack the virus in different ways.
